Of this line Nora Crook remarks: ‘ “Emily” holds out the promise of lost early love restored’ (‘Shelley
and Women’ in The Oxford Handbook of Percy Bysshe Shelley 65–82 (75)). Youth’s vision recalls the Poet’s
dream of the ‘veilèd maid’ in Alastor 151–91.

Nbk 17 p. 48 reads: I love thee . . . though to you I cannot be/Lover or brother. The subsequent draft reads:
I [love thee canc.] though by no [conceded canc.] name/Is it [permitted canc.] to declare the same. — Cp.
